config.description: Single-variable follow-up to v011: same soft mask, same 3-epoch schedule, but the periodic recurrent-state reset fires every 2,000 rows instead of every 4,000.
config.hypothesis: The reset period is a knob, not a threshold, and 2,000 rows beats 4,000. dozken's public reset2k scores 0.6569 against their reset4k, so shortening our horizon should gain rather than cost. Mechanism: across 20k rows the recurrent state degrades (their Q1 0.70 -> Q4 0.638) and a zero state beats the model's own 10k-row state, so more frequent resets keep the model nearer its best regime. If 2,000 instead loses to 4,000 then the horizon is near-optimal at 4,000 and this lever is spent.
config.change_vs_parent:
Shorter absolute reset horizon: 4,000 rows -> 2,000 rows. Implemented as chunk_len 2000 -> 1000 with state_reset 4000 -> 2000. Unchanged: the soft mask (loss.mask_model), aux weighted-MSE 0.05, EMA 0.999, architecture 2x128 (192,258 params), seed 1337, 3-epoch cosine schedule.
WHY chunk_len MUST MOVE TOO, and the resulting confound: the trainer enforces state_reset = k * chunk_len with k >= 2, because a reset at every chunk boundary would discard all carried state and silently leave the model with no memory beyond one chunk. At chunk_len 2000 the shortest legal period is therefore 4000, which is exactly v011's value, so a shorter horizon is unreachable without also halving chunk_len. Keeping k=2 preserves the 2-chunks-of-carry ratio the trainer enforces and changes the absolute horizon from 4,000 to 2,000, which is also dozken's literal reset period. The confound is that chunk_len sets truncated-BPTT granularity, so this run is not a pure period change; a (chunk_len 2000, state_reset 6000) run would isolate the ratio and test the opposite direction. 1000 divides 20,000 exactly, so no chunk crosses a sequence boundary.
